projects.name: Umm Shaif Gas Cap Development
projects.location: Umm Shaif field and Das Island, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: FID $6.2bn (AED 22.6bn); three EPC packages totalling $5.1bn plus a $365m ADNOC Drilling contract
projects.scope: Development of the Umm Shaif gas cap to unlock more than 600 mmscfd of gas plus associated liquids (around 10% of current UAE gas demand): two 30,000-tonne offshore gas compression systems and new gas inlet and processing facilities on Das Island, with 14 new wells drilled over 18 months.
projects.why_it_matters: The largest new offshore gas award in the UAE this year. It opens multi-year fabrication, drilling and Das Island brownfield work and bridges ADNOC's gas self-sufficiency target with its global LNG ambitions.

projects.name: Rich Gas Development Phase 3 — Ruwais NGL Train 5
projects.location: Ruwais, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: EPC contract $4.3bn; part of the $13.2bn three-phase RGD programme
projects.scope: A fifth NGL fractionation unit at the Ruwais NGL complex with gas treatment, sweetening, propane refrigeration and storage, adding around 23,000 tonnes a day (roughly 8 mtpa) of NGL product capacity for export.
projects.why_it_matters: One of the largest single downstream-gas EPC awards in the Gulf in 2026. It monetises rising rich-gas volumes into export NGLs and feeds the TA'ZIZ and Borouge petrochemical hub.

sources.title: MEED — Tecnimont breaks ground on Ruwais NGL train 5 project (24 Sep 2026)

projects.name: Rich Gas Development Phase 2 — Habshan Gas Train
projects.location: Habshan, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: EPC $3.9bn (about $4.04bn including a 220 kV switch station)
projects.scope: A new 670 mmscfd natural gas processing train at the Habshan complex, including gas pipelines, separation and condensate stabilisation, acid gas removal, deep NGL recovery units and a 220 kV switch station.
projects.why_it_matters: The largest contract in Wison's history and a clear signal that Chinese EPC contractors are now winning ADNOC's flagship onshore gas trains.

projects.name: Upper Zakum 1.5 Million bpd Expansion
projects.location: Upper Zakum field, 84 km offshore Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Est. more than $10bn per trade reports; package values not disclosed
projects.scope: Three EPCI packages to lift Upper Zakum output from 1.2 to 1.5 million bpd: new offshore processing facilities, wellhead platforms, utilities, water injection, pipelines and brownfield tie-ins across the four-island network, integrated with the Project Lightning HVDC electrification.
projects.why_it_matters: The single biggest offshore oil award in the region this cycle. It underpins ADNOC's 5 million bpd capacity goal and locks up Gulf fabrication-yard and marine-installation capacity for several years.

projects.name: Umm Shaif Long-Term Development Plan 2.1 (Oil Expansion)
projects.location: Umm Shaif field, c.150 km north-west of Abu Dhabi, with new facilities on Das Island
projects.value_note: Not disclosed; the preceding LTDP-2 phase was reported at c.$2bn (press est.)
projects.scope: Two main EPC packages to sustain Umm Shaif oil output at around 390,000 b/d with a 430,000 b/d peak: offshore water-injection and ESP wellhead towers, riser platform, manifold and flare towers, bridges, flowlines, main oil line, water-injection and gas export pipelines and subsea cables; a new combined artificial island with two 135,000 b/d separation trains, two 275 mmscfd gas compression and dehydration trains, produced-water treatment and water injection; plus an optimised crude stabilisation train on Das Island. Expression-of-interest exercise completed in June 2026; ADNOC Offshore is weighing early contractor engagement before the main EPC tender.
projects.why_it_matters: The next multi-billion-dollar offshore oil package after Upper Zakum and Lower Zakum, and the third phase of a programme that previously went to NMDC Energy (LTDP-1, $946m) and McDermott (LTDP-2). Early contractor engagement would signal ADNOC's preferred bidders well before tender.

MEED - Contractors express interest in next phase of Umm Shaif oil field expansion (9 Jun 2026)

projects.name: Bab Gas Cap Development
projects.operator: ADNOC with TotalEnergies, BP, CNPC, JODCO, ZhenHua, GS E&P
projects.location: Bab field, onshore Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Est. $8bn for the main gas plant EPC package per MEED and Upstream; overall investment not disclosed and FID not yet taken
projects.scope: Development of the gas cap at the Bab oil field, described as the world's largest gas cap development, targeting around 1.5 bscfd of natural gas (about 15% of ADNOC Gas's processing capacity) for domestic supply and LNG feed. ADNOC Gas has tendered a processing plant for up to 1.85 bscfd of raw gas in four EPC packages (main plant, early civil works, pipelines and non-process works); technical bids for the main plant are due 16 November 2026, extended from 17 July. Separately, ADNOC Onshore invited bids in October 2026 for a well tie-in package, estimated at more than $800m, covering the gas-producing and gas-injection wells at Bab.

contractors.name: TotalEnergies 10%, BP 10%, CNPC 8%, JODCO 5%, ZhenHua Oil 4%, GS E&P 3%

projects.why_it_matters: The main plant EPC, estimated at $8bn, is the largest live gas tender in the UAE. Four international consortia are bidding, and ADNOC Gas says it will move prudently before taking FID, so award timing is the key variable to watch after Umm Shaif. The $800m-plus well tie-in tender launched in October adds a second large live package for onshore EPC contractors.

MEED — Adnoc Gas to move prudently on Bab gas cap project (10 Aug 2026)

projects.name: Ruwais LNG Export Project
projects.operator: ADNOC / Ruwais LNG with Shell, BP, TotalEnergies and Mitsui
projects.location: Al Ruwais Industrial City, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: EPC contract $5.5bn; ADNOC Gas to acquire a 60% stake for an estimated $5bn in 2028
projects.scope: A 9.6 mtpa lower-carbon LNG export plant with two 4.8 mtpa electric-drive liquefaction trains running on clean grid power, more than doubling UAE LNG capacity to over 15 mtpa. Around 90% of capacity is already contracted long-term.
projects.why_it_matters: The UAE's first new LNG export trains in decades. The 2028 schedule is the critical path for the Estidama, pre-conditioning and Habshan compression works.

projects.name: ADNOC New Onshore LNG Liquefaction Facility (4 mtpa, east-coast site bypassing Hormuz)
projects.location: Fujairah, on the Gulf of Oman outside the Strait of Hormuz (per trade press, referred to as East Coast LNG); c.160 km feed-gas pipeline from Habshan
projects.value_note: Est. more than $5bn per Upstream (press estimate); not disclosed by ADNOC
projects.scope: Single-train 4 million t/y liquefaction plant with CO2 removal, dehydration, mercury removal and sulphur reduction, LNG storage tanks, boil-off gas handling, export jetty and utilities, plus a c.160 km feed-gas pipeline and additional compression at the Habshan complex. Being procured through a FEED-to-EPC design competition. ADNOC scheduled a site visit for the FEED-to-EPC competitors in October 2026.
projects.why_it_matters: A second UAE LNG export plant sited outside the Strait of Hormuz would add 4 mtpa of chokepoint-free capacity on top of Ruwais LNG's 9.6 mtpa, directly answering the 2026 Hormuz disruption. The FEED contest is structured so the winning design house takes the EPC, so the eventual award could rank among the UAE's largest energy contracts of 2026–27.

projects.name: Al Mandous Underground Crude Storage Expansion (Phase 2)
projects.location: Al Mandous, Fujairah, on the Gulf of Oman outside the Strait of Hormuz
projects.value_note: Not disclosed; Phase 1 EPC (three 14m-barrel caverns) was $1.21bn, awarded to SK E&C in 2019
projects.scope: Second phase adding about 25 million barrels of underground rock-cavern crude storage to the existing 42 million-barrel, three-cavern Al Mandous complex. ADNOC issued an expression of interest in April 2024, put the project on hold in June 2025 and has now revived it after completing a new contractor prequalification exercise in 2026; the main EPC tender has not yet been issued.
projects.why_it_matters: Revived in the wake of the 2026 Hormuz disruption, the expansion would lift strategic crude storage on the UAE's east coast by around 60%, complementing the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline and the planned east-coast LNG plant. A specialist cavern-construction package with few qualified contractors.

projects.name: ADNOC Refining Capacity Enhancement and Sustainable Aviation Fuel Projects (Technip Energies)
projects.location: Abu Dhabi (site not specified in the announcement; ADNOC Refining's main complex is Ruwais)
projects.value_note: Not disclosed
projects.scope: Two contracts signed with Technip Energies on 20 October 2026 during the UAE-France Business Dialogue: one for a refining capacity enhancement project and one for a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) project. Scope, capacities and schedule have not been published.
projects.why_it_matters: First disclosed step in a new refining investment cycle at ADNOC Refining after the Ruwais crude flexibility project, and a formal SAF project following the refinery's 2023 ISCC certification for co-processing. Details of the capacity uplift will determine the size of the follow-on EPC market.

projects.name: Habshan–Al Nouf Sales Gas Pipeline (EWEC Mirfa Relocation and AI Data Centre Phase 2)
projects.location: Habshan to Al-Nouf, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Est. more than $417m: Kalpataru disclosed a UAE gas pipeline EPC award of over INR 40bn without naming the client, and MEED sources link it to this contract; ADNOC Gas has not disclosed a value
projects.scope: A 127 km, 56-inch sales gas pipeline from the Habshan gas compression complex to a new customer receiving station at Al-Nouf, with four block valve stations, custody metering and pressure-regulation facilities and tie-ins to the Meram and Estidama package 3 lines. It is sized to deliver 600–660 mmscfd for phase 2 of an Abu Dhabi AI data centre and 650–715 mmscfd for EWEC's relocated Mirfa power assets.

contractors.name: Kalpataru Projects International
contractors.role: EPC (per MEED sources; company confirmed an unnamed UAE gas pipeline award on 28 Sep 2026)

projects.why_it_matters: A direct link between the UAE's AI data-centre build-out and gas infrastructure spending: roughly half of the line's capacity is earmarked for an AI campus's power supply. The 31-month EPC schedule points to completion in 2029, and Kalpataru is understood to have beaten bidders including CPP, Arkad and Galfar Emirates.

sources.title: MEED — Adnoc Gas awards EPC contract for Ewec sales pipeline (1 Oct 2026)

projects.name: SARB Deep Gas Development
projects.location: Satah Al Razboot (SARB) field, c.60 km south-east of Das Island, offshore Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Est. c.$500m EPC (MEED estimate); ADNOC has not disclosed a value
projects.scope: Greenfield development of deep gas reservoirs at the SARB field producing around 200 mmscfd: two unmanned wellhead platforms, a gas export pipeline to new inlet facilities on Das Island with pig receiver, power and fibre-optic cables from Al Qatia, Bu Sikeen and Zirku islands, and brownfield tie-ins at Al Qatia, Bu Sikeen, Das, Zirku and Arzanah islands.
projects.why_it_matters: A smaller but fast-moving piece of ADNOC's gas self-sufficiency push: FID and the EPC award came together in January 2026 and McDermott cut first steel in October 2026, nine months later. Bidders beaten included NMDC Energy and Saipem; MEED Projects lists completion in May 2029.

projects.name: Nasr-115 Expansion (Nasr Phase 2 Full Field Development)
projects.location: Nasr field, c.130 km north-west of Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: $942m EPC per MEED
projects.scope: Engineering, procurement, construction and installation of two topsides, a new manifold tower, a jacket, a bridge and associated pipelines, plus high-speed subsea cables and brownfield modifications, to lift Nasr oil capacity to 115,000 b/d.
projects.why_it_matters: One of the offshore brownfield packages feeding ADNOC's 5 million b/d crude-capacity target for 2027; more than 55% of the contract value is expected to flow back into the UAE economy under ADNOC's In-Country Value programme.

sources.title: MEED — McDermott wins $942m Adnoc Offshore field expansion contract (23 Jan 2026)

projects.name: Bu Hasa–Shuaiba Enhanced Oil Recovery Unit 1 (Phase 1)
projects.location: Bu Hasa field, c.200 km south of Abu Dhabi city
projects.value_note: Not disclosed
projects.scope: Hybrid contract for the first phase of tertiary recovery in the Shuaiba reservoir: a lump-sum EPC scope for the complete pipeline system from East Hub to the separation plant, plus call-out works for water-alternating-gas (WAG) injector and water-supply-well tie-ins. CO2 flooding was identified in earlier studies as the leading EOR option; ADNOC targets a 70% uplift in production and a 70% ultimate recovery factor.
projects.why_it_matters: A test case for CO2-based EOR at scale in ADNOC's largest onshore field (650,000 b/d capacity), linking the Habshan CCUS build-out to incremental oil. The tender was issued on 20 September 2026 and technical bids, first due 8 October, were extended to 17 October.

sources.title: MEED — Adnoc Onshore seeks bids for Bu Hasa field EOR project (16 Oct 2026)

projects.name: Rumaitha and Shanayel Field Facilities Project
projects.location: Rumaitha and Shanayel fields, onshore Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Not disclosed
projects.scope: On-plot and off-plot facilities to enhance and sustain oil production from the Rumaitha and Shanayel fields at 45,000 b/d. ADNOC Onshore received expressions of interest in January 2026 and contractors were preparing commercial bids in October 2026.
projects.why_it_matters: A mid-sized onshore brownfield EPC that keeps the 5 million b/d capacity programme moving at ADNOC's smaller north-east fields while the giant Bab and Bu Hasa expansions run; a likely target for regional EPC contractors below the tier-one bracket.

sources.title: MEED - Contractors prepare prices for Adnoc Onshore field facilities project (20 Oct 2026)
MEED - Adnoc Onshore receives interest for field facilities project (9 Jan 2026)

projects.name: Hail and Ghasha Ultra-Sour Gas Development
projects.operator: ADNOC with Eni, PTTEP and OMV
projects.location: Al Dhafra offshore artificial islands and onshore Ruwais, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Est. around $17bn total EPC; $11bn structured financing closed December 2025
projects.scope: Four artificial-island drilling centres, offshore structures and subsea pipelines plus onshore gas processing, sulphur recovery and CO2 handling to produce over 1.5 bscfd of gas while capturing 1.5 mtpa of CO2, targeting net-zero operational emissions.
projects.why_it_matters: The UAE's largest gas project and the world's first sour gas development targeting net-zero operations. The $11bn financing shows how ADNOC funds megaprojects off balance sheet.

projects.name: Lower Zakum Long-Term Development Plan 1
projects.location: Lower Zakum field, offshore Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Est. $7.5bn across three EPC packages per MEED; NMDC Energy package confirmed at $2.64bn
projects.scope: Three EPC packages to raise oil production capacity at Lower Zakum, building on the earlier $975m artificial island G and $548m main gas line works that support a 450,000 bpd target and 700 mmscfd of associated gas handling.
projects.why_it_matters: Together with Upper Zakum it forms a $17bn-plus offshore oil build-out that keeps UAE fabrication yards and installation fleets fully booked into the late 2020s.

projects.name: Rich Gas Development Phase 1 — Habshan, Das Island, Asab and Bu Hasa
projects.location: Habshan, Das Island, Asab and Bu Hasa, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: $5bn of EPCM contracts: Wood $2.8bn, Petrofac $1.2bn, Kent $1.1bn
projects.scope: Brownfield upgrades and debottlenecking across four complexes, including two new 420 mmscfd dehydration and compression trains at Das Island and expansion of Habshan and Habshan 5, to increase rich gas throughput and liquids recovery.
projects.why_it_matters: First phase of the $13.2bn RGD programme and a large EPCM rather than lump-sum opportunity set; Petrofac's participation is being watched closely after its 2025 administration.

projects.name: Ruwais LNG Feed Infrastructure — Pre-conditioning Plant, Pipelines and Compression
projects.location: Habshan 5 and the Habshan–Ruwais corridor, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: $2.1bn in three EPC awards (Enppi/Petrojet $1.24bn, CPP $514m, Petrofac Emirates $335m) plus a separate $330m Habshan compressor plant
projects.scope: An LNG pre-conditioning plant at Habshan 5 to treat around 1.5 bscfd of feed gas for Ruwais LNG, a 26 km suction and 155 km discharge pipeline from Habshan to Ruwais, and new booster and compression trains at Habshan.
projects.why_it_matters: These feed-gas works must land before Ruwais LNG's 2028 start-up, so any slippage here directly threatens first-cargo timing.

projects.name: TA'ZIZ Methanol Plant
projects.location: TA'ZIZ Industrial Chemicals Zone, Ruwais
projects.value_note: EPC $1.7bn (AED 6.2bn); $2bn project financing closed May 2026
projects.scope: A 1.8 mtpa methanol plant powered by clean grid electricity, one of the world's largest and most energy-efficient methanol units, and part of TA'ZIZ Phase 1's 4.7 mtpa chemicals build-out.
projects.why_it_matters: With financing closed and a Korean EPC on site, it is the most bankable of the TA'ZIZ derivatives projects and a template for the financed joint-venture model ADNOC is applying across Ruwais chemicals.

projects.name: TA'ZIZ Low-Carbon Ammonia Plant
projects.operator: TA'ZIZ with Fertiglobe, Mitsui and GS Energy
projects.location: TA'ZIZ Derivatives Park, Ruwais
projects.value_note: EPC value not disclosed
projects.scope: A 1 mtpa (3,000 t/d) low-carbon ammonia plant on a 10.8 ha site, targeting marine fuel and export ammonia markets with CO2 captured for storage; reported as approaching completion in May 2026.
projects.why_it_matters: The UAE's first merchant low-carbon ammonia export plant and the first physical proof point for ADNOC's hydrogen and ammonia strategy.

projects.name: Borouge 4 Polyolefins Complex
projects.location: Al Ruwais Industrial City, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Total project cost $6.2bn per Borouge
projects.scope: A 1.5 mtpa ethane cracker plus 1.4 mtpa of new polyethylene capacity, including two Borstar PE units and the XLPE 2 wire-and-cable plant, making Ruwais the world's largest single-site polyolefins complex at around 6.4 mtpa.
projects.why_it_matters: B4 is the swing asset behind the ADNOC–OMV Borouge Group International merger; its staged 2026 start-up adds roughly 1.4 mtpa of polyethylene to Gulf export supply. The 100,000 t/y XLPE 2 wire-and-cable unit made its first commercial deliveries in September 2026, the first B4 unit to reach market.

sources.title: Hydrocarbon Processing — Borouge International commercializes XLPE products from new Borouge 4 UAE plant (10 Sep 2026)

projects.name: Borouge EU2 Cracker Expansion and PE4/PE5 Debottlenecking
projects.location: Al Ruwais Industrial City, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: EU2 EPC value not yet disclosed; FEED complete, EPC award planned in 2026
projects.scope: Upgrade of the second ethane cracker to add around 230,000 t/y of olefins and polyolefins by end-2028, alongside expansion of the PE4 and PE5 units from 540,000 to 700,000 t/y each by Q1 2027.
projects.why_it_matters: The EU2 EPC award is the main live petrochemical tender in the UAE this year and a near-term opportunity for cracker-revamp specialists.

projects.name: Habshan Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage
projects.location: Habshan gas complex, Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: EPC $615m; total project cost not disclosed
projects.scope: Carbon capture units at the Habshan gas plant, CO2 pipeline infrastructure and a network of injection wells to capture and permanently store 1.5 mtpa of CO2, tripling ADNOC's capture capacity to 2.3 mtpa.
projects.why_it_matters: The largest CCUS build in MENA to date and the enabler of ADNOC's low-carbon gas and ammonia marketing; delivery risk rose after Petrofac entered administration in 2025.

projects.name: ESTIDAMA Gas Transmission Network Expansion
projects.location: UAE-wide sales gas network; Habshan compression hub
projects.value_note: Packages awarded to date total around $2.4bn; programme est. around $3bn per MEED
projects.scope: Expansion of the UAE sales gas pipeline network from around 3,200 km to over 3,500 km with a new gas compression plant at Habshan and dedicated lines to Ruwais LNG, increasing customer reach and transmission capacity.
projects.why_it_matters: A multi-package, in-country-value-heavy pipeline programme that keeps local contractors busy and ties every new gas source into the Ruwais export and domestic grid.

projects.name: Bab and Bu Hasa Onshore Oilfield Expansion
projects.location: Bab and Bu Hasa fields, onshore Abu Dhabi
projects.value_note: Contract value not disclosed
projects.scope: EPCM for construction and expansion of surface facilities at Bab (+91,000 bpd to 541,000 bpd) and Bu Hasa (+100,000 bpd to 750,000 bpd), plus retooling at Northeast Bab and the South East asset, over a 4.25-year term.
projects.why_it_matters: The main onshore leg of ADNOC's 5 million bpd capacity push, and confirmation that CPECC has become the incumbent brownfield EPCM contractor at Abu Dhabi's giant onshore fields.
